title: Which Berlin Pass Is Worth It? - Quick Summary
items: **There is no single best pass.** The Berlin cards split by what they cover: transport cards (WelcomeCard, CityTourCard) give rides and discounts but no free museums; the Museum Pass Berlin gives 30+ museums but no transport; single and day tickets are often cheapest for a short, walkable trip.

**Know the benchmark: the 24-hour AB day ticket is €11.20 in 2026.** A single AB ride is €4.00. A 72-hour CityTourCard is €35.60, which works out to about €11.87 a day, so a transport card is not automatically cheaper than paying as you go.

**Museum-heavy trip? Buy the Museum Pass Berlin (€32).** It covers 30+ museums over three days, including the Museum Island museums that are open. Pergamonmuseum is currently closed. The pass includes no transport, so pair it with day tickets or walk.

**Transport-heavy trip? Compare the partner lists before buying.** The WelcomeCard costs €28.50 for 48h or €39.50 for 72h AB and has 170+ discount partners. The CityTourCard costs €35.60 for 72h AB and advertises discounts at 30+ partners.

**Short, central, walking trip? Skip the passes.** Berlin is walkable, and a few single tickets plus a day ticket when you ride a lot usually beats any card. My free walking tour route stays inside the normal AB zone.
**The Deutschlandticket (€63/month) is a subscription, not a tourist pass.** It only makes sense for long or very transport-heavy stays, not a two- or three-day city break.
